domain: observatory telescope time allocation and rescheduling rules

Allocation_Rules: R1: Each approved proposal holds the standard grant in Cycle unless a Panel message sets a different cap for that proposal.
R2: A Completed night is charged at its observed time; where the time is recorded in minutes, divide by 60 to get hours.
R3: A Weather_Lost night is charged at its scheduled hours in full.
R4: An Equipment_Fault night and a Cancelled_By_PI_Before_Night entry are charged nothing.
R5: Charged hours are computed from the log as it stands on the date in question, using the latest status recorded for each night.
R6: A reschedule request must be lodged at least 7 calendar days before the booked night. The gap is the later calendar date minus the earlier one; the time of day is ignored.
R7: A Panel exemption from R6 applies only to the booked nights it names, and a later Panel message can revoke it for booked nights on or after a stated date.

R8: An additional-night request is granted in full when charged hours plus the requested scheduled hours do not exceed the cap. If they exceed the cap and the hours left under the cap are at least 4.0, only those hours are granted, as a shortened night. If fewer than 4.0 hours are left, the request is declined. The night must also show as free in the Instrument_Schedule.
R9: A cap change or exemption made by Panel message applies only while no later Panel message withdraws it.
R10: At cycle close, granted hours less charged hours are unused hours and return to the shared pool.

state.regulation_1_1_scope: These regulations apply to every interment, memorial and permit within Randfell Municipal Burial Ground and to any plot held under a grant of exclusive right of burial. Where a grant has lapsed, the burial office must be consulted before any booking is accepted, and any booking may then proceed only on the terms the superintendent sets out in writing. Permit accounts are opened in the name of the applicant and remain open until every charge on them has been settled or credited.
state.regulation_2_4_records: The register of interments is the sole record of who lies in each plot and of the personal details entered against each burial. A correction to the details of a person already entered must be made through the registrar's correction process. Once a correction is registered, the corrected detail governs all fee calculations, notices and permits issued after the date of registration, and the superseded detail must not be used for any further charge.
state.regulation_3_1_credits: Credit notes raised on a permit account are set against the total of all charges on that account, together with any deposits held, and are not refundable in cash. The balance shown on the latest statement is the amount payable.
state.regulation_3_2_deposits: A deposit taken at booking is held against the permit account and is set against the total charges once those charges have been raised. Deposits are not refunded where the booking proceeds to interment.
state.regulation_4_1_excavation: Grave excavation is arranged by the grounds team on the working day before the interment. The grounds team may move the excavation by one working day where ground conditions require it, and must tell the applicant's contact by the end of the working day before the revised date. Excavation is not carried out on Sundays or public holidays.
state.regulation_5_2_transport: Transport permits are issued by the registrar for the movement of remains to the cemetery. A transport permit is not a charge on the burial account and does not affect the fee band for the interment.
state.regulation_6_2_wording_approval: Superintendent approval of proposed memorial wording may be given in writing, by e-mail, or in person. The superintendent's office records each approval on the permit file when it is received, and the applicant is told the file reference.
state.regulation_6_4_carving_start: Carving of any inscription must not begin until written approval of the approved wording has been placed on the permit file. Contractors must show the file reference to the grounds team before the carving slot is used.
state.regulation_7_1_memorial_size: Headstones on lawned plots must not exceed the dimensions set in the memorial schedule and must be set on a concrete foundation laid by a registered contractor. Kerbs and vases are permitted only where the schedule allows them for the section. Foundations are inspected by the grounds team before the memorial is set.
state.regulation_8_3_appeals: Any person may ask the superintendent to review a decision on fees or permits within twenty working days of that decision. Review requests must be made in writing, are logged on the permit file, and do not suspend the due date of any charge unless the superintendent says otherwise in writing.

PART 1. ALLOCATION POLICY (rev. 3, adopted 2026-04-20)

1.1 Scheduling unit. One scheduled night on the Munhaven 1.0 m reflector is 8.0 observing hours. Allocations are recorded in hours and quoted in nights; one night equals 8.0 h.

1.2 Charging. A night that runs to completion with no weather or fault loss is charged at its full scheduled length. A night affected by weather is charged at its full scheduled length less whatever is returned under 1.3.

1.3 Weather returns. The return for a weather-affected night is set by the usable hours in the reduced data log, using only the reduction version marked FINAL by the telescope engineer. Usable hours below 4.0 h: the whole scheduled night is returned. Usable hours of 4.0 h or more but below 8.0 h: half the scheduled night (4.0 h) is returned. Usable hours of 8.0 h or more: nothing is returned. Once a later reduction version is marked FINAL, earlier versions are superseded and are not used.

1.4 Extensions. An extension to an allocation takes effect only when the chair of the Time Allocation Committee confirms it in writing on the register thread. Suggestions by the scheduler, the proposer or the engineer do not change the allocation.

1.5 Telescope faults. A night lost to a fault in the telescope or its instruments is returned in full, provided the fault is entered in the engineering log on that night.

1.6 Reruns of returned time.
(a) [rev. 2, 2025-11-14] A rerun of returned time must be booked within 60 days after the date the telescope returned to service, as recorded in the engineering log.
(b) [rev. 3, 2026-04-20] Where a weather return is set at half-night level under 1.3(b), the returned half night is carried into the next semester block as a separate request, and rule 1.6(a) is not applied to that request. Whether a separate request needs a fresh application form has been referred to the rules sub-group, which has not yet reported.

1.7 Deadlines. Proposals close on the published closing date. A resubmission that changes only the title does not change the original submission date.

1.8 Precision. Usable hours are recorded to two decimal places and compared with the thresholds in 1.3 exactly as recorded.

1.9 Rebooking requests. A request to rebook returned time must name the prop_id and the scheduled date of the lost night, and must state which rule it relies on.

state.notes: Charging rule OBS-AL-4: an allocated night is charged as one full night when observed, or when cancelled by the holder with less than 48 hours' notice before its scheduled dusk. Notice runs from the logged cancellation time to the scheduled dusk time of that night, in local time. A cancellation with 48 hours' notice or more releases the night without charge. Nights closed for weather are not charged and return to the balance. A cancellation withdrawn before its night has no effect on charging or on the late-cancellation count. Late cancellations are counted by the calendar year in which they were logged; two or more in the review year move the holder to reduced priority for the next cycle, and counts from earlier years are not carried forward. The review year for this record is 2026. Each charged night is valued at the hours per night in force on that night's scheduled dusk date. Email from Bramo Gakeckson dated 2026-03-12 asked whether night 11 could move to a later dusk; no change has been entered.

§4.1 Height. A memorial needs a structural certificate from a qualified engineer before a permit can issue if its total height above ground level, counting any base or plinth that stands above ground, is more than 1.20 m. Kerbs set flush with ground are not counted.

§4.3 Installation window. The installation day must fall no later than 42 calendar days after the permit issue date, or no later than 56 calendar days after it where a structural certificate is on file at permit issue. The issue date is not counted, so day 1 is the calendar day after issue.

§4.5 Superseded sheet. The 2024 fee sheet (height surcharge GBP 20) is withdrawn and must not be quoted to applicants.

Subject: Semester 2026B allocation rules, weather losses and the position of programme MS-114

PURPOSE
This memo restates the allocation rules in force for Semester 2026B and records where programme MS-114 (Mortwallica Survey Group, lead Wendus Jalcanley) now stands. The register holds all figures in minutes, not hours. Programme MO-207 (Morvuckica Cosmology Consortium) appears in section 4 for completeness only; it is not part of the MS-114 position.

1. RULES IN FORCE
1.1 Allocations are made in whole nights. One nominal night is 480 minutes of telescope time.
1.2 Weather loss. Time lost to weather is refunded only for a night on which the total weather loss is more than 90 minutes. The refund for such a night is the total weather loss minus 90 minutes. All weather entries for the same night are added together before the 90 minutes is deducted, and the 90 minutes is deducted once per night only. Weather entries on different nights are never combined.
1.3 Cancellation by the programme. A run cancelled by the programme is returned in full where the cancellation notice is given at least 14 calendar days before the first night of the run. Calendar days are counted from the date of the notice to the date of the first night, with no adjustment for weekends or public holidays. Where the notice is shorter, the run is charged in full, unless the cancellation was caused by an instrument fault recorded in the Engineering Desk log for the run dates. A fault recorded for other dates does not count.
1.4 Moves by the observatory. A run moved by the observatory keeps its full number of nights.
1.5 Nights removed at programme request. Where a programme asks for nights to be removed from a run, the removed nights are returned in full if the removal is approved before the first night of the run as currently scheduled. Otherwise they are charged.
1.6 Net charged time. A programme's net charged time is its total allocated minutes on the register, less weather refunds under 1.2, less returns under 1.3 and 1.5.

policy.scope: Weather and technical losses on scheduled nights for approved programmes.
policy.night-definition: A night is identified by the calendar date on which its scheduled session starts. Loss intervals that run past midnight belong to that same night.

domain: cemetery plot burial-right renewal and interment booking charges

regulation_extracts.text: An exclusive right of burial runs for the term stated on its grant, counted from the grant date, and lapses at the end of the day before the anniversary of the grant date unless it is renewed.
A right may be renewed by an application received no more than 12 months before it lapses. A renewal term runs from the day after the lapse date and takes effect once the renewal fee has been paid.

An interment needs at least 3 clear working days' notice. Notice runs from the day a complete signed application is received. Clear days exclude the day of receipt, the day of interment, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.
An interment on a Saturday carries an out-of-hours surcharge of 185.00 GBP. The Registrar may waive the surcharge by written approval, and a waiver covers the surcharge only.
Interment charges are the interment fee, the grave opening fee and any out-of-hours surcharge still payable. Memorial permit fees are charged on a separate booking.
Where the registered holder has died, an application may be made by the personal representative named in a grant of probate for the holder's estate.

PART 1. BURIAL REGULATIONS EXTRACT (Regulations 2025, as amended)

4.1 Exclusive right of burial. An exclusive right of burial is granted for 50 years from the grant date. Its expiry date is the day before the 50th anniversary of the grant date.

4.2 Renewal. A renewal of an exclusive right of burial takes effect from the day after the previous right expires and runs for a further 50 years.

4.3 Lodging of renewal applications. As adopted in 2025, a renewal application must be lodged with the Trust at least 30 days before the expiry date. This requirement is subject to any later amendment recorded in the Trust minutes.

4.4 Interments in lapsed plots. No interment may be made in a plot whose exclusive right of burial has expired, unless a renewal application was lodged in time under section 4.3 and the interment takes place within six months after the expiry date.

4.5 Interment types. Charges are set by type:
(a) new_grave_full: a coffin or body interment into a grave not previously used.
(b) new_grave_ashes: cremated remains placed in a grave not previously used.
(c) reopening: any interment into a grave in which an earlier interment already lies, whatever the form of the remains.

4.6 Working days. A working day is a Monday to Friday that is not a public holiday on the Trust holiday calendar. For any two dates, the count of working days is taken over the days strictly after the first date and strictly before the second date.

4.7 Changes of date. Where an agreed interment date is changed, the change is treated as a new booking made on the day the change is agreed.

4.8 Late booking. A late-booking surcharge applies where fewer than five working days fall between the booking date and the interment date, counted under section 4.6.

4.9 Renewal fees. Renewal fees are invoiced separately and are not part of any interment charge.

4.10 Memorials. A memorial permit is needed before any headstone or kerb is installed. Memorial permits do not affect the interment charge.

4.11 Depth and vaults. Cremated remains are placed at least 0.6 metres below the surface unless the registrar directs otherwise. A vault is not required for cremated remains.

4.12 Opening hours. Interments take place Monday to Friday from 09:00 to 16:00 and on Saturdays from 09:00 to 12:00, subject to the Saturday supplement in the fee schedule.

4.13 Records. Register entries and correspondence are kept for 30 years after the last interment in a plot.

Regulation_Extract.Title: Reopening of graves and fee tiers
Regulation_Extract.Reopening_Notice_Rule: A grave that already holds an interment may not be reopened for a further interment unless at least 10 clear calendar days' notice has been given in writing to the registered holder of the exclusive right of burial. A clear day excludes both the day on which the notice is given and the day of the interment.
Regulation_Extract.Shortened_Notice_Rule: The notice period may be reduced to 7 clear calendar days where the registered holder gives written consent to the shorter period and the signed consent is entered on the grave record before the interment takes place. Consent given after the interment has no effect on the notice period.
Regulation_Extract.Fee_Tier_Rule: The resident tier applies where the deceased was ordinarily resident within the Weasfell district at the date of death. Otherwise the non-resident tier applies. The Weasfell district includes Frouckgate and does not include Stirthorpe. Residence is taken from the most recent written evidence held on the file.
Regulation_Extract.Revised_Notice_Rule: Where a fee notice was calculated on a tier that no longer applies, the registry must issue a revised fee notice for the applicable tier before the interment is recorded as complete. Any balance is payable against the revised notice.
Regulation_Extract.Exclusive_Right_Term: An exclusive right of burial runs for 50 years from the date of grant. The term ends on the anniversary of the grant date falling 50 years later.
Regulation_Extract.Gravedigging_Hours: Interments may take place Monday to Friday between 09:30 and 15:30, and on Saturdays between 09:30 and 12:00. No interments take place on Sundays or public holidays.
